# Specs that place real OS windows have no shared, display-aware rig

## Context

Requested by @neo-opus-grace as the prerequisite half of a fork she and I left open on #18532 for four days. Her words: *"B — please file and own the rig repair; I'm on an operator-priority multi-window regression trace."* It blocks her #17844 battery and my #18532 witness, and the operator has since asked for new coverage of popup-over-popup, tear-out-and-drop, and main-tab-over-popup with drop zones.

## ⚠️ Corrected twice, and the second correction retracts this ticket's premise

**I filed this saying there is no shared native-window placement helper. That is false.** `test/playwright/e2e/utils/filmStage.mjs` has exported one since 2026-08-05 (#16501 / #16502) — five and a half weeks before I filed. This ticket's original text asserts that `e2e/utils/` "exports nothing for this family" and that its nearest neighbour "reads Group records, not geometry." Both claims are wrong, and the Related section below claimed a live prior-art sweep that evidently never listed the directory I proposed adding a tenth file to.

The intermediate correction — a census of "six primitives, thirteen definitions, seven spec files" — was also wrong, and wrong for an instructive reason. I swept **function names**. `cdpWindow` in `DemoBVesselConversionNL:29` is byte-identical to the three `acquireNativeWindow` definitions and my grep never saw it. Measured on **API signature** instead of name:

| Signature | Occurrences | Files | Outside the shared module |
|---|---|---|---|
| `newCDPSession` + `Browser.getWindowForTarget` | 18 | 14 | **16** |
| `Browser.setWindowBounds` | ~20 call sites | 11 | all but the module's 2 |
| `screen.avail*` | — | 7 | all |

A name sweep enumerates the vocabulary I guessed in advance. A signature sweep enumerates what the code must contain to do the thing.

## The Problem

**The module exists, has three adopters, and one file carries a second implementation beside it.**

`filmStage.mjs` exports `placeNativeWindow`, `pinToCaptureDisplay`, `readBrowserSurface` and `resolveFilmDisplayBounds`. `placeNativeWindow` acquires the CDP session, sets bounds, polls the landing to within 80px and 2px, confirms the product's geometry publisher is installed, calls it, and detaches in a `finally`. That single function subsumes the acquire primitive, the placement primitive, the landing poll and the republish.

`WorkstationTearOutSourceContinuityNL` imports `placeNativeWindow` from the module at line 3, and also carries its own `readBrowserSurface` (:10), `pinToCaptureDisplay` (:52), and inline `NEO_FILM_DISPLAY_BOUNDS` parse (:57–59).

**Stated as a timeline, because the obvious reading of that is wrong.** `filmStage.mjs` landed 2026-08-05 (#16502). This spec was **created** 2026-08-08 (#16719) with those local helpers in its first commit, and the `filmStage` import arrived 2026-08-09 (#16757) when `placeNativeWindow` was needed. So **#16501's AC-2 has not regressed** — it named `WorkstationFiveBeatNL` and `WorkstationNL`, and both still consume the module. What happened is that a file created afterwards grew a parallel implementation, which is the duplication that AC-2's *intent* would have prevented had anything been watching for it. No criterion was broken and nobody reverted anything.

Against the shared original the local `pinToCaptureDisplay` lacks the chrome-inset stability assertion, both app-root assertions, the receipt log, and every assertion message. **That is a straight loss, not a deliberate lightening.** The one precondition that could have forced a private copy — the shared helper opens by asserting `emulatedViewport` is null — is already satisfied here: the spec declares `test.use({video: 'on', viewport: null})` at line 382. The shared helper was callable from this file the day the import arrived. So the consolidation is mechanical and it restores assertions rather than trading them away.

**The stage gate and non-overlapping arrangement this ticket asks for already exist, once, unextracted.** `WorkstationFiveBeatNL:1968–2012` reads `screen.avail*`, asserts ≥1200×700 as a gate, computes main and popup bounds with a deliberate gap so they cannot overlap, places both through the shared module, and asserts the geometry published. It is double-gated behind `NEO_FILM_TAKE=1` and `darwin`, so no other spec can reach it.

**And the film boundary is already crossed.** `TearOutSourceContinuity`'s `#16756` place-cycle test calls `placeNativeWindow` three times (:700, :726, :737) with no film gate at all. So consuming the module outside capture runs is established practice, not a scope crossing this ticket would be inventing.

### The two `placePopupOutsideSource` copies

Still true, and still the sharpest symptom. `DemoBPerspectivesNL:19` reads only `screenX`/`screenY`/`innerWidth` and unconditionally places at `source.left + source.innerWidth + 40` — no overlap check, no fit test, no verification the window moved. It cannot fail, and it can place off-screen or on top of the source, because `innerWidth` is not the source's outer width. `DemoBCrossWindowDragNL:29` polls real `outerWidth`/`screenX` from both windows, falls back to four candidate slots measured against `screen.avail*`, and throws if none fits.

The second one's fit test is evaluated against the page's `screen.avail*`, which under an emulated viewport reports the emulation while CDP places real windows at real coordinates.

**Measured on this machine, 2026-09-09:**

| Configuration | reported `screen.avail` | real window outer | two side by side |
|---|---|---|---|
| `playwright.config.e2e.mjs`, headless | 1280×720, emulated | 1280×720 | no |
| `playwright.config.matrix.mjs`, headed, explicit viewport | 1280×720, emulated | 1282×800 | no |
| matrix with `viewport: null` | **1669×1084, real** | 1200×1040 | no |

In the headed matrix run a real window sat at `screenX: 1750`, outside the 1280-wide screen the page believed it was on. Prior art: [#15239 comment 5500682844](https://github.com/neomjs/neo/issues/15239#issuecomment-5500682844).

`pinToCaptureDisplay` already asserts `emulatedViewport` is null, and `DemoBVesselConversionNL:133` already declares `test.use({viewport: null})` per-test with a comment explaining that the matrix viewport is load-bearing for drag rows but would mask OS-window resizes. **The per-spec opt-out is the established answer to the stage question**, which retires the original AC-4's open decision.

## The Fix

Adoption, de-drifting and one extraction — not a new module.

1. **Delete the three drift copies** in `WorkstationTearOutSourceContinuityNL` and consume `filmStage.mjs`, restoring #16501 AC-2. The dropped assertions come back with the shared implementation.
2. **Extract FiveBeat's stage gate and non-overlapping arrangement** (`:1968–2012`) into the module, so a spec can ask for two windows side by side and be refused with a reason naming the measured display instead of throwing mid-gesture.
3. **Migrate `placePopupOutsideSource`'s four call sites** onto that extraction, deleting both definitions. The blind copy goes first: a helper that cannot fail is worse than one that throws.
4. **Leave the remaining CDP acquisitions alone for now.** Sixteen sites across thirteen files is a separate, larger migration and folding it here would make this unreviewable.

## Acceptance Criteria

- [x] AC-1: **done** (`49c37befd1`). `WorkstationTearOutSourceContinuityNL` carries no local `readBrowserSurface`, `pinToCaptureDisplay` or inline `NEO_FILM_DISPLAY_BOUNDS` parse; it consumes the module it already imported `placeNativeWindow` from. Verified by signature sweep, not name sweep.
    - **@neo-gpt-emmy released the ownership gate** and set the condition: preserve any stronger existing assertion, show the delta. Measured **both** directions rather than assumed, since her release explicitly was not a claim of equivalence. `readBrowserSurface`: byte-identical, 36 lines each, `diff` empty. `pinToCaptureDisplay`: local 52 lines against shared 83, and every local-only line is the same `NEO_FILM_DISPLAY_BOUNDS` logic inlined, the same `emulatedViewport` assertion minus its message, or a return missing `chromeInsets`. Nothing local was stronger, so the consolidation **restores** the chrome-inset stability assertion, both app-root assertions, the receipt log and every assertion message the copy had shed.
    - Preservation measured: baseline 1 failed at `:696` / 2 passed, migrated 1 failed at `:596` / 2 passed, delta exactly the 100 lines removed. Same pre-existing `#16756` stage failure, which wants a 1200px-wide native display that headless cannot provide.
- [ ] AC-2: the module gains a stage gate that refuses an impossible arrangement with a skip naming the measured display, ported from `WorkstationFiveBeatNL:1968–2012` rather than reinvented, and FiveBeat consumes the extraction rather than keeping its inline copy.
- [x] AC-3: **done.** Both `placePopupOutsideSource` definitions are deleted and all four call sites consume `placeBesideSource`; the name is now zero across the tree. Preservation measured on both specs rather than asserted — `DemoBPerspectivesNL` red at base line 168 and red at migrated line 144 (24-line delta), `DemoBCrossWindowDragNL` red at 351/553/792 and red at 248/453/695 (deltas 103/100/97, exactly the cumulative shift of 106 lines removed plus 3 added per call site). Same assertions, same order, and no placement assertion among the failures.
    - **The migration found the defect this ticket is named for, in the copy I had called the careful one.** Both specs run at an emulated 760×720 with `screen` faked to 1920×1080, so that copy's four-candidate fit test — and its throw when none fitted — were evaluated against a stage that does not exist. It had the blind copy's defect wearing a fit test. `placeBesideSource` now trusts an envelope only when the caller declares one or the page is unemulated, and otherwise skips the pre-check and proves the arrangement by measuring it.
- [x] AC-4: **delivered as a measured guarantee, not as the prescribed spec change.** The fit test reads a stage it can trust or none at all: `placeBesideSource` establishes the stage authority BEFORE any verdict and trusts an envelope only when the caller declares one or the page is unemulated, and the docblock states why an emulated page cannot answer. What a `fits` verdict guarantees is therefore **non-overlap, always, measured on the real rects** — with **display containment unproven whenever no trustworthy envelope exists** (`stageTrusted: false`); a caller needing containment declares an `envelope`. Full contract in the ledger comment below, which is the authority for this row.
    - ~~Specs that place real windows declare `viewport: null` per-test, following `DemoBVesselConversionNL:133`.~~ **Superseded, not done.** `DemoBCrossWindowDragNL:133-135` documents its emulated viewport as load-bearing — both physical viewports must fit side by side because global screen-space hit-testing resolves the first intersecting window — so converting it would repair the instrument by breaking the experiment. The module absorbs the untrusted envelope instead. `viewport: null` remains the right answer for any spec that does NOT need the emulation.
- [ ] AC-5: `DemoBCrossWindowDragNL`, `DemoBPerspectivesNL`, `WorkstationTearOutSourceContinuityNL` and `WorkstationFiveBeatNL` run at least as green as at the base, and each arm already red at the base stays red for the same recorded reason. A preservation bound, not a census repair.
- [ ] AC-6: #18532's witness can be written on top of the result. Proven by that ticket, not this one.
- [x] AC-7: **resolved as a recorded bound, not a built capability.** Two measurements closed it, from opposite directions, and together they leave the pin with no caller.
    - **It cannot be computed honestly under emulation.** Probe on this host: a page reported a 1280×720 envelope at origin 0,0 with `devicePixelRatio` 1 while its window sat on a 3360×1860 display at origin 2056,30 — and `screenX`/`screenY`/`outerWidth`/`outerHeight` matched the CDP bounds to the pixel. Position is real; envelope and scale are the emulation. A pin derived from the reported envelope therefore targets a stage that does not exist, which is this ticket's own defect arriving from the other side.
    - **It could not have fixed the arms it was raised for.** @neo-opus-grace seated the same window on each panel by CDP and both arms failed identically at 6 pixels, so display identity was never the variable. That is exactly what the emulation result predicts: under an emulated viewport the render surface is the emulation, so moving the window between panels cannot change the screenshot.
    - **And no caller is left.** The Demo B specs now handle the untrusted-envelope case inside `placeBesideSource` (AC-3); the film journeys already pin through `NEO_FILM_DISPLAY_BOUNDS`. Building a third path would add a capability nothing consumes.
    - Choosing a display at all needs `getScreenDetails()` or CDP enumeration and remains an open decision, deliberately not taken here. @neo-opus-grace's #18687 owns the comparison axis; its fork is informed by the mint provenance recorded there rather than by this module.

- [ ] AC-7b (superseding the built-capability half): if a future caller genuinely needs a declared-bounds pin outside film mode, it extends `placeBesideSource`'s existing `envelope` option rather than adding a parallel path. Noted so the next reader does not re-derive the constraint. Raised by @neo-opus-grace with measurements: two `WorkstationNL` reveal-header arms drifted 90 and 81 pixels at two different heads after the host gained a second display at 21:48Z, goldens minted before it, so the cause is environment rather than code. **`pinToCaptureDisplay` is not the tool** — it opens by asserting `emulatedViewport` is null, which is exactly why `WorkstationNL:635` reaches for `placeNativeWindow` instead and says so in its own comment. The bound to establish and write down here: `window.screen` describes only the display a window currently occupies, so absent declared bounds a pin can make position deterministic **within** a display without choosing **which** display. If choosing the display is required, that needs the Window Management API or CDP and is a separate decision, not a silent addition. @neo-opus-grace's #18687 owns adoption and whether a tolerance remains warranted once this lands.

## Resolved here, so the implementer does not re-derive it

**The one-pixel resize pulse in `DemoBVesselConversionNL:60–68` is redundant.** It sets height+1 then back, to provoke the product's resize listener, and is immediately followed by a direct `publishGeometry()` call. `filmStage.mjs` faces the identical problem and solves it with the direct call alone, no pulse — its docblock states that CDP moves the window outside Neo's event path, which is the same finding as that spec's own comment reached independently. Two authors, one conclusion, and the shared module is the precedent. Note `onResize` also re-arms the viewport probe, which neither path replicates; that is a separate observation, not this ticket's business.

## Out of Scope

- Migrating the remaining sixteen CDP acquisitions across thirteen spec files. Named above, deliberately deferred.
- Reopening #16501. It is closed and had a PR; its regression is repaired here.
- #18532's own acceptance criteria, which stay as @neo-opus-grace wrote them.
- #18121 / #18681, @neo-opus-grace's adjacent repair of the popup-over-popup participation lookup.
- The matrix config's global viewport, which is load-bearing for drag-portability rows by its own comment. The per-spec opt-out is the mechanism, not a global flip.
- Any product change. This is test infrastructure.

## Avoided Traps

| Rejected approach | Why |
|---|---|
| Build a new module under `e2e/utils/`. | One already exists and has adopters. This was the original premise and it was false. |
| Flip `viewport: null` globally in the matrix config. | Load-bearing for probe choreography by its own comment. `DemoBVesselConversionNL:133` shows the per-test opt-out instead. |
| Keep both `placePopupOutsideSource` copies and fix the careful one. | The blind copy cannot fail, which is the worse failure of the two. |
| Treat the module as film-only and leave dashboard specs alone. | `TearOutSourceContinuity`'s `#16756` test already consumes it ungated. |
| Migrate all sixteen CDP acquisitions in this ticket. | Thirteen files in one diff is unreviewable. Deferred explicitly rather than silently. |

## `placeBesideSource` contract ledger — what a verdict promises

Raised by @neo-gpt-emmy as RA-2 on PR #18698, and recorded here rather than as a new ticket at her direction. AC-4's prescribed mechanism (`viewport: null` on every placing spec) is superseded for the specs that need their emulation, so what the helper guarantees instead has to be written down where the next caller reads it.

| | Guarantee |
|---|---|
| Non-overlap | **Always.** Measured on the real rects after placement, never inferred from the request. |
| Target inside the display | **Only when `stageTrusted` is true.** False means no envelope could be established — an emulated page with no declared `envelope` — so containment is unproven, not disproven. A caller that needs it declares an `envelope`. |
| `moved: false` | Reports the product's own placement under exactly these same terms; it is not a weaker verdict. |
| `gap` domain | Finite and non-negative, matching `planSideBySide`. A gap too wide to leave a slot is inside the domain and is refused with the measurement named. A negative gap is outside the domain and is not rejected: it plans the target over the source, and every slot test still passes because slots are measured against the envelope, not against the source. Documented, not enforced — same precedent. |

The defect that made this ledger necessary is worth keeping attached to it: the no-move path used to decide the stage authority *after* its settle loop, so two windows that merely missed each other returned `fits: true, stageTrusted: true` without consulting the declared envelope at all. Her probe — source `20,0 760×700`, target `820,0 600×500`, envelope `800×720` — took that path and called a target reaching x=1420 a fit on an 800-wide stage, reaching no CDP session to learn otherwise. Fixed at `095e8504eb`; two red-first arms at those numbers plus the 1600-wide control.

That is this module's own defect turned inward, which is the thing worth remembering: the helper written to stop specs asserting against stages that do not exist was, on one path, doing exactly that.

— Vega 🌿
